name: Commit Queue
description: Async git-commit serialization pipeline. Converts commit serialization from a synchronous per-agent mkdir-mutex on a shared index (which chokes the fabric under high commit concurrency -- head-of-line-blocked sessions, a 60s-timeout 'commit storm', and a fragile shared-index contamination guard) to an asynchronous single-consumer queue modeled on the graph-update SQS/Lambda pattern, adapted for a LOCAL repo (the consumer is a local commit-worker daemon, not a cloud Lambda, because the git repo is on-disk). Agents enqueue a commit-request via the byte-for-byte-preserved safe-commit.sh interface (1338 callers) and a single concurrency=1 worker owns all git-index access -- structurally eliminating the contamination race, the timeout-storm, and blocked sessions, while preserving every gate (sensitive-leak, owned-paths, ds-gate, author identity, atomic per-agent commit).
phase: 3 TOs issued; TO-4 (observability/alarms) and TO-5F (contamination-guard retirement + worker gate re-assert) are both COMPLETE, closed 2026-07-07 with live-exercised evidence (not config-read): TO-4 proved a real worker-killed alarm fire + DLQ alarm fire + a real SNS subscriber; TO-5F proved owned-paths rejection, non-compiling-.py rejection (catching 2 real self-fixed bugs), and confirmed the legacy contamination apparatus was never ported into the queue path. TO-1/TO-2/TO-3 landed via direct commits without their own formal TO files. THE CORE GOAL IS NOT YET REALIZED: the commit queue is fully built + tested but has never been switched on fabric-wide -- every agent commit still runs through the old lock-based system. The load test (TO-6R) proving many-agent concurrent commits work is built but deliberately locked pending explicit leadership sign-off, gated on a scheduled low-activity window; the 1,338-caller fabric-wide rollout hasn't started. As of 2026-07-07, leadership confirmed the queue is still dormant and made finishing this cutover a priority.
blocking: TO-6R (load test) gated on a CPU/quiet-activity window sign-off (COO self-monitoring, not yet cleared as of this pass). Fabric-wide rollout of the 1,338 commit-trigger call sites is the actual remaining goal-critical work, sequenced after TO-6R.
pipeline: fabric-infra (local commit-worker daemon + local durable queue; CloudWatch for observability only)
